Erase Large Water Bodies from Polygons

Source: R/erase_water_bodies.R
erase_water_bodies.Rd

Removes sea and lakes from polygons using a land/water mask, so that statistics of the territory (elevation, cropland, emissions per km2) are not diluted by water in shoreline or lake units.

Usage

erase_water_bodies(
  poly,
  water,
  land_value = 100,
  min_km2 = 50,
  buffer = 0.5,
  iteration = NULL
)

Arguments

poly

A SpatVector of polygons.

water

A SpatRaster land/water mask, in the CRS of poly.

land_value

Value of land cells in water; every other non-NA value is water. Default 100, as in GSHHS.

min_km2

Smallest water body erased, km2. Default 50.

buffer

Buffer around poly when cropping water, in the map units of poly. Default 0.5.

iteration

optional character to be print before computation. Usually, it is the name of the object on which the function is applied. This is useful when the function is used inside an apply family function to keep track of the iterations.

Value

poly with the water bodies erased, attributes kept.

Details

The mask is cropped around the polygons, every cell that is not land_value is turned into water polygons, and the water polygons of at least min_km2 are erased. Smaller patches stay part of the units: a coarse mask only resolves large lakes anyway, and this drops single-cell noise.

With the GSHHS land/water mask of the spatial repository (geophysical/land_water_mask/GSHHS, ~3 km), land is 100 and water 0. At that resolution the mask can cut a few km off a coastline, so a very small coastal unit can lose much of its area.

A polygon entirely under water disappears from the result. Compare the row counts, or match on an id, to find it.

See also

terra::erase(), crop_with_buffer()

Examples

water <- terra::rast(xmin = 0, xmax = 2, ymin = 0, ymax = 2, res = 0.5,
                     crs = "epsg:4326", vals = 100)
water[1:2, 1:2] <- 0  # a water body in the top-left corner
p <- terra::vect(terra::ext(0, 2, 0, 2), crs = "epsg:4326")

terra::expanse(p, unit = "km")
#> [1] 49231.58
terra::expanse(erase_water_bodies(p, water), unit = "km")
#> [1] 36922.69
